commit.message:
QUIC: covering CRYPTO frame retransmission may induce use-after-free in record layer

Function quic_read_record() obtains data from a QUIC stream via a call
to ossl_sframe_set_peek(), which peeks at data in the receive stream
buffer.  The _peek() caller receives a pointer into the receive stream
buffer.  The read offset is not advanced, so the data in the buffer
are considered not yet consumed.

The quic_read_record() function is called by ssl3_read_bytes() to read
TLS protocol messages, to process either handshake or key update
messages.  The pointer used by the SSL record layer becomes stale
(i.e., it refers to freed memory) if the QUIC stack receives a stream
frame that overlaps the range from which bytes were retrieved
by the _peek() operation: the insertion process replaces that range,
releasing the old buffer and substituting it with the newly received
one.

The fix reintroduces a range locking mechanism that allows the record
layer to mark bytes retrieved by the _peek() operation as locked.
This allows the stream reassembly module to identify and discard
overlapping bytes in a newly received stream frame before they
are joined to the range.  This completely avoids overlap between
ranges, so the join operation of two ranges never needs to discard
the buffer.

Fixes: CVE-2026-95691
